subtopics.title: The Intrusion Family — Batholith to Sill

questions.question: A DISCORDANT intrusion is one that:
options: Cuts ACROSS the layering of the country rock — like a dyke or a batholith
Lies parallel between the strata
Erupted onto the surface as lava
Contains no minerals

questions.question: Intrusive igneous rock is coarse-grained because:
options: It cooled instantly in the air
SLOW cooling deep underground gave large crystals time to grow
Wind sorted its grains
It was deposited layer by layer in water

questions.question: The laccolith and the lopolith are told apart by:
options: The laccolith cutting across the strata
The lopolith having no known floor
The laccolith ARCHING the overlying strata up into a blister, while the heavy lopolith SAGS the strata beneath it into a saucer
Their identical shapes

questions.question: The Bushveld Igneous Complex north of Pretoria is:
options: A chain of young volcanoes
A dolerite dyke swarm
The country's largest canyon
The world's largest LOPOLITH, whose layered saucer supplies most of the planet's platinum

subtopics.title: From Buried Intrusion to Standing Landform

questions.question: An intrusion becomes visible scenery when:
options: Erosion strips its cover and the harder igneous rock then RESISTS while the softer country rock wastes away
The magma melts its way upward again
Earthquakes throw it onto the surface
Rain dissolves the granite

questions.question: A resistant dyke in softer country typically stands as:
options: A round bald dome
A long, narrow, dead-straight WALL of rock striding across the landscape regardless of hills and rivers
A saucer-shaped basin
A horizontal cliff band at one level

questions.question: At Howick the Umgeni River plunges ninety-five metres because:
options: The river crosses a soft clay bed
A dam wall collapsed there
The river pours over the resistant edge of a dolerite SILL, which forms the waterfall's lip
Wind eroded a hollow in the valley

questions.question: On the map, dyke and sill are opposites because:
options: Both follow the rivers
Both form circular patterns
The sill is always a straight ridge
The dyke runs as a straight ridge IGNORING drainage and contours, while the sill's cliff line CLINGS to one contour level

questions.question: Pressure release, or unloading, occurs when:
options: Erosion removes the overburden, the load on the deep granite falls, and the rock expands slightly
Rainfall soaks into the summit and adds weight
The granite is reheated by the sun
Ice sheets press down on the mountain

questions.question: Sheet joints are:
options: Vertical cracks caused by earthquakes
Curved fractures PARALLEL to the land surface, opened by the granite's expansion as it unloads
Layers of sediment inside the granite
Cracks made by plant roots only

questions.question: Exfoliation makes a granite dome MORE rounded because:
options: Wind polishes the summit flat
The rock melts in the sun
The shed sheets are CURVED, so every slab lost leaves a smoother, rounder surface beneath
The dome grows new rock each year

questions.question: A large isolated exfoliation dome standing over an erosion plain is called:
options: A tor
A lopolith
A pediment
A BORNHARDT — like Spitzkoppe over the Namib gravel plains or the granite heads of the Lowveld

questions.question: Joints matter to tor formation because they:
options: Divide the buried granite into rectangular blocks and let water in to rot each block from its cracks inward
Stop all weathering from happening
Carry lava to the surface
Only form after the boulders are exposed

questions.question: Corners of a buried granite block decay fastest because they are:
options: Made of softer minerals than the faces
Attacked from THREE directions at once, while edges get two and faces only one
Closest to the surface
Always wet while the faces stay dry

questions.question: A corestone and its grus are:
options: A volcanic bomb and its ash
Two unrelated rock types
The hard rounded survivor of a joint block, and the crumbly rotten granite that decayed around it
A fossil and its cast

questions.question: The strict order of the two-stage theory of tors is:
options: Stripping first, then underground rotting
Both stages happen at the surface
Volcanic eruption first, then freezing
Joint-guided chemical rotting FIRST, underground; stripping and exposure SECOND

questions.question: In the concrete-pour picture, the full underground pour with no known bottom is the:
options: BATHOLITH — the monster granite mass bulldozing across every layer
Sill
Laccolith
Dyke

questions.question: The pocket pour that jacked its ceiling up, and the pour that bowed its floor down, are:
options: Dyke and sill
LACCOLITH (blister, arched roof) and LOPOLITH (heavy saucer, sagged floor)
Batholith and dyke
Sill and batholith

questions.question: Concrete up a vertical crack against concrete between two boards gives:
options: Two batholiths
A lopolith and a laccolith
A DYKE (buried wall, discordant) and a SILL (buried shelf, concordant)
Two volcanoes

questions.question: The two-word test that sorts all five intrusions on a diagram is:
options: Hot or cold
Big or small
Old or young
Lies WITH the layers (concordant) or CUTS across them (discordant)

questions.question: The monstrous backpack the granite carries stands for:
options: The weight of the overlying rock, whose removal by erosion lets the granite expand
The granite's own crystals
The rainfall on the summit
The plant cover on the dome

questions.question: The granite cracks like orange peel, meaning:
options: Random cracks in every direction
Curved shells parallel to the surface, nested one inside the next
A single straight crack down the middle
Cracks only at the base

questions.question: Peeling perfects the dome rather than destroying it because:
options: The mountain regrows its lost rock
The peels protect the summit from rain
A curved peel can only come off a curve — every shed slab leaves the mountain rounder than before
Wind rebuilds the slopes with sand

subtopics.title: Soap Blocks and the Secret of the Stacked Boulders

questions.question: In the soap-crate picture, the dripping tap water stands for:
options: Groundwater creeping along the joints and rotting each block from its cracks inward
A river flowing over the koppie
Lava rising through the granite
The wind sandblasting the boulders

questions.question: Each soap cube rounds into a ball because:
options: The water is warm
Corners dissolve from three sides at once, edges from two, faces from one — corners always lose first
The cubes were round to begin with
The crate squeezes them round

questions.question: A tor is best described as:
options: A tower built up by volcanic eruptions
Boulders rolled together by a flood
A stack of survivors LEFT BEHIND when erosion stripped the rotten grus from around the corestones
A pile made by glaciers

questions.question: The joint-spacing rule says:
options: Close joints make domes and wide joints make tors
Joint spacing has no effect on landforms
All granite becomes tors eventually
WIDE joint spacing lets the mass smooth into a DOME; CLOSE spacing rounds small blocks into corestones that stack as TORS
